boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cane Hill (Boston Mountains) record (November 28, 1862) in Prairie Grove Campaign [November 1862]. The pursuit from Cane Hill through Boonsborough to the Cove Creek defile is one record; Jewell's November 23 reconnaissance and the December 4-6 outpost skirmishes before Prairie Grove are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Department of Missouri [US] and two cavalry brigades [CS], with no numerical bounds; the live field reads zero. Britton says Blunt learned on the 24th that Marmaduke had seven thousand cavalry and some artillery, and that Blunt marched on the 27th at the head of five thousand men and thirty pieces of artillery; he names Marmaduke's division as Shelby's, MacDonald's and Carroll's brigades, Bledsoe's six-gun battery and a company of Quantrill's men. Shelby lists his brigade as three regiments, Elliott's scouts and Quantrill's company, with two iron 6-pounders under Bledsoe, and says the Federals had at least twelve guns on his position and vastly superior numbers.
claims.rationale: An intelligence estimate, a march strength, unit lists and an interested impression of relative numbers. Britton's three brigades differ from the frozen two. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Britton describes a Confederate line on high ground with timber behind it, a later line behind a low ridge with a deep ravine in front, a mountain too steep for field batteries except along the road, and the narrow Cove Creek valley between mountains rising perhaps a thousand feet, where the fight ended at a defile; he says the ground was too rough for cavalry. Shelby says his gun on the Fayetteville road stood on an elevated position and that the ground on the mountain did not allow forming by regiments or squadrons. NPS places the final stand on Cove Creek.
claims.rationale: Ground described by a history and an interested report; no map inspected. The positions were chosen during the running fight.

claims.rationale: Stated aims from a summary, a history and an interested report.

claims.value: Britton says Blunt reconnoitred Marmaduke's position, directed the batteries and flanking columns, and at the defile called for volunteers, Jewell leading the charge in which he was mortally wounded; Marmaduke's flag of truce, carried by MacDonald, ended the day. Shelby says Marmaduke ordered him to fall back after he reported infantry turning his left, and that the general was everywhere on the field. NPS names Shelby's brigade as the one that fought the delaying action. The frozen commanders are Brigadier Generals John S. Marmaduke and James G. Blunt; the live page lists Marmaduke without a rank.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate tactical victory and the live result Confederate Victory (tactical). Britton describes successive Confederate withdrawals ending in a truce, after which Marmaduke retreated toward Van Buren and Blunt returned to Cane Hill. Shelby says the last Union charge was sent back in confusion, ending the day. NPS says the Federals withdrew to Cane Hill while the Confederates returned to Van Buren.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The labels differ in emphasis from Britton's account of repeated Confederate retreats.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 475 total (US 40; CS 435); the live field reads 85 (US 40; CS 45). Britton relays Blunt's report of four killed and thirty-six wounded, and of seventy-five Confederates killed and mortally wounded left on the ground, adding that the Confederate wounded carried off are not known. Shelby does not state his brigade's losses, saying they were already reported.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen CS 435 and live CS 45 have no inspected basis.

open_questions: Curtis's and Blunt's reports (Nos. 1-2), Cloud's, Ellithorpe's, Bassett's, Hopkins's and Ewing's reports (Nos. 3-7), Carroll's and MacDonald's reports (Nos. 8, 10), the Union casualty return and any Marmaduke report on Cane Hill remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume I (Putnam's, second edition, revised, 1891) is a retrospective history whose title page says it is based upon the official reports of named Federal and Confederate commanders; its preface says the author served with the Federal army in that section and almost invariably took the official reports as a guide for numbers and casualties. It is not independent of the Official Records families and is treated as partly a participant's interested Union account. Shelby's December 1, 1862 report on Cane Hill and Hindman's December 1862 dispatch and report on Prairie Grove are separate author families of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
